benchmark_gaps: CRISPR off-target scoring is simplified (GC content + k-mer complexity only) — no CFD/MIT/CRISPRater position-specific mismatch penalties or seed-region weighting
CRISPR on-target efficiency uses heuristic GC/poly-T/G-bonus — no Doench Rule Set, Azimuth, or deep-learning efficiency models
No support for alternative PAM specificities (NAG/NGA for SpCas9 variants, TTTV for Cas12a, NGGNG for xCas9)
No guide ranking/selection algorithm — all guides returned without prioritization by combined on/off-target score
No self-complementarity or hairpin formation check for guide RNA
No homopolymer detection beyond poly-T (poly-A, poly-C, poly-G not penalized)
No genome-wide off-target search capability — only scores guides against the input sequence
No guide RNA secondary structure prediction (U6 terminator compatibility, scaffold stability)
Variant SIFT score is binary (conservative vs radical substitution) — no real conservation-based scoring from homologous sequences
Variant PolyPhen score uses only amino acid property changes — no structural features (SIFT, Grantham distance, domain impact)
No Grantham distance calculation for missense variant severity
No splice site prediction (donor/acceptor site disruption, exonic splicing enhancer/silencer)
No regulatory region annotation (promoter, enhancer, UTR, silencer, insulator)
No variant prioritization framework (CADD-style integrated score)
No VCF parsing/writing — variants only as dataclass objects
No variant normalization (left-alignment, parsimonious representation)
No protein domain impact assessment for missense variants
No codon usage bias consideration in variant effect prediction
No mitochondrial variant prediction (mitochondrial codon table, heteroplasmy)
No clinical variant classification (ACMG/AMP guidelines)
No variant frequency filtering (gnomAD-style population frequency)
No compound heterozygote or de novo variant detection
No somatic vs germline variant classification

bottlenecks: CRISPR module is 274 lines with only one class — no separation of concerns between guide design, scoring, and filtering
Variant module is 306 lines with monolithic predictor — no pluggable scoring strategies or annotation sources
Structure module is 156 lines with only Chou-Fasman secondary structure — no tertiary structure, contact maps, or disorder prediction
Network module is 256 lines with only co-expression — no regulatory network, TF binding, or miRNA target prediction
No shared sequence/alignment utilities — each module reimplements basic sequence operations
No caching or memoization for expensive computations (off-target searches, structure prediction)
No async/parallel processing for batch variant prediction or genome-wide guide design
No plugin architecture for adding new scoring models or annotation sources
No configuration system for thresholds, weights, and model parameters
No integration with external databases (KEGG, UniProt, PDB, gnomAD, ClinVar)
No data models for metabolic pathways, phylogenetic trees, or regulatory networks
No serialization/deserialization for analysis results (JSON, HDF5, database)
No progress reporting or cancellation for long-running analyses
No result persistence or caching layer
No event-driven pipeline for chaining analyses (variant → structure → network)
No validation of input sequences (alphabet checking, ambiguous base handling)
No logging or metrics collection for analysis performance
No error recovery or partial result return on failure
No API rate limiting or resource quotas for external service calls
No versioning of analysis results or reproducibility tracking
missing_algorithms: Metabolic pathway analysis: KEGG pathway mapping, metabolic network reconstruction, flux balance analysis (FBA), metabolic control analysis, pathway topology scoring

Phylogenetic analysis: sequence alignment (Needleman-Wunsch, Smith-Waterman), multiple sequence alignment (ClustalW, MAFFT, MUSCLE), tree building (neighbor-joining, UPGMA, maximum likelihood, Bayesian), evolutionary distance calculation (Jukes-Cantor, Kimura, Grantham), positive selection detection (dN/dS), phylogenetic footprinting

Tertiary structure prediction: 3D structure prediction (AlphaFold-style), contact map prediction, disordered region prediction, protein folding, molecular dynamics simulation, protein structure alignment, protein-ligand docking

Regulatory network analysis: transcription factor binding prediction, promoter analysis, enhancer prediction, miRNA target prediction, cis-regulatory element detection, chromatin accessibility prediction, 3D genome organization (Hi-C), gene regulatory network inference, feed-forward loop detection, network motif discovery
Sequence analysis: BLAST-like search, motif discovery (MEME, Gibbs), gene prediction, ORF finding, repeat masking, primer design, sequence logo generation

Variant analysis: VCF parsing, variant calling, variant annotation (ANNOVAR-style), splice site prediction, variant prioritization (CADD-style), clinical variant classification (ACMG), structural variant detection, copy number variation, tandem repeat expansion, mobile element insertion

Population genetics: Fst, Tajima's D, nucleotide diversity, linkage disequilibrium, haplotype analysis, phasing, imputation, kinship matrix, heritability estimation, variance components, mixed models, BLUP/GBLUP

Genomic selection: genomic prediction models, marker-assisted selection, QTL fine mapping, multi-trait GWAS, epistasis detection, genotype-environment interaction, machine learning for genomic prediction

Protein analysis: protein structure prediction, protein design, enzyme engineering, protein-protein interaction prediction, epitope prediction, signal peptide cleavage, transmembrane domain prediction, post-translational modification prediction, protein stability prediction
Expression analysis: differential gene expression, RNA-seq analysis, qPCR analysis, single-cell transcriptomics, gene set enrichment, pathway enrichment
Comparative genomics: synteny analysis, ortholog/paralog identification, gene family analysis, genome evolution, horizontal gene transfer detection
Epigenomics: DNA methylation analysis, chromatin accessibility (ATAC-seq), histone modification analysis, 3D genome organization
Synthetic biology: genetic circuit design, biosensor design, metabolic engineering, biosafety assessment, biocontainment, gene drive design
Safety assessment: allergenicity prediction, toxicity prediction, anti-nutrient prediction, digestibility prediction, substantial equivalence, compositional analysis, GMO detection and quantification
